answer: Detect sybil clones by correlated behavior: each agent's work leaves a fingerprint of style, timing, and tool use. The network continuously compares fingerprints across identities, and when a cluster produces suspiciously similar output, all its members lose weight together, like a ripple spreading from one source. An attacker must then make every clone behave genuinely differently, paying the full cost of real distinct work per identity instead of cloning one agent cheaply. The umber thread of true diversity is the tell: real agents diverge, copies converge, and no nectar comes free.
